Yes, let's go to the residence immediately.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is completely safe.
You are absolutely right.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: It's an important question.
I have important business.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.
It is time to make our move before influential people.
The governor met with an influential politician.

meanings.en: to head, lead, take charge of

examples.trans: What ministry specifically will you head?
The experienced general took charge of the army.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зможность'). Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'possibility, opportunity, resource' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You have some possibilities.
This is a great opportunity.

examples.text: Но ты же ректор! У тебя есть какие-то возможности.
examples.trans: But you're the rector! You have some possibilities.
There, look.
Here's my toy car.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Even a child knows.
Even Mum doesn't know.
Yes! Even a child knows.

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: lowest part of a body of water

examples.trans: Found him on the bottom of the river.

examples.text: Рыбаки потом нашли его на дне.
examples.trans: Fishermen later found him on the riverbed.

examples.text: Я видела, как он идёт на дно.
examples.trans: I saw how he was going to the bottom.
Why are you hovering over me?
A kind soul.

examples.text: У меня на душе сильная тревога.
examples.trans: I have a strong anxiety in my soul.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.
Let's go!

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.trans: But you've still got some.
But I know.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.
When will you finish work?

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.
This is a gold ring.
He's very good with his hands.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: for movement; где is for location

examples.trans: Where are you going?
And where are you going?
Wait, where are you two going?
What ministry specifically are they offering me?
The official works in the ministry of finance.
What ministry specifically will you head?
They are considering you for the post of minister.
The new minister held the first meeting.

examples.text: Тебя всерьёз рассматривают на пост министра.
examples.trans: They are seriously considering you for the post of minister.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!
Where exactly are we heading right now?
The car was heading toward the railway station.
Where are you heading right now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'медленно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Release him immediately!
Go home at once.
What bribe? Release him immediately!

обозначиться.gloss: to make a move, show oneself

meanings.en: to make oneself known, assert presence

examples.trans: You must urgently make your financial move.
The candidate quickly asserted his presence before the leadership.
It is time to make our move before influential people.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.trans: Our chances are huge.
Thank you so much!

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: + genitive or accusative: я не ожидал = I didn't expect (that)

examples.trans: I didn't expect that.
We are expecting guests.
Arkasha, I didn't expect that. Thank you!
A letter from Mum.
I'm tired of work.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: a door, window, bottle, or business

examples.trans: I'm going to open it now.
They open the shop at nine.
I am opening return fire!
I'm standing in front of you.
There's a car in front of the house.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'present, gift' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a present for you.
Thank you for the present!

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)

examples.trans: We'll go home.
Let's go!
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.
Great, congratulations!
Happy holiday to you!
Great, congratulations.

meanings.note: + infinitive: Пора идти = Time to go

examples.trans: Time to go home.
It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.
That's not a problem.
I have a problem.
I know the problems of ordinary people.
Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?
Let's go to the residence immediately.

examples.text: В загородной резиденции состоялся важный приём.
examples.trans: An important reception took place at the country residence.
Yes, let's go to the residence immediately.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: relating to fish or fishing industry

examples.trans: The ministry of fisheries of the whole country!

examples.text: На обед подали вкусный рыбный суп.
examples.trans: Delicious fish soup was served for lunch.

examples.text: Посмотрим, какой из тебя рыбный мастер.
examples.trans: Let us see what kind of fish master you are.
I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
Summer is coming soon.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'начала').

examples.trans: First they were rude and insulting over there.
Let's start everything from the beginning.

examples.text: Мы танцевали. Сначала они там грубили, оскорбляли.
examples.trans: We were dancing. First they were rude and insulting over there.
He became mayor.
You've changed.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трана'). Common feminine noun meaning 'country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you!
It is a big country.

examples.text: Над тобой вся страна смеётся! Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you! Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?
Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Удачи! = Good luck! (genitive: 'I wish you luck')

examples.trans: Good luck to you!
That's a real stroke of luck.

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.
This is a law of federal significance.
The federal service is conducting the investigation.
The Federal Security Service is operating here!
The ministry of fisheries develops the industry.

examples.text: Фермер успешно ведёт своё сельское хозяйство.
examples.trans: The farmer successfully runs his agriculture.
The ministry of fisheries of the whole country!

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
